title: The captain from Bolton who helped with Titanic rescue

evidence_packet.title: The captain from Bolton who helped with Titanic rescue
evidence_packet.lead: Arthur Rostron was the captain of RMS Carpathia when it received a morse code message from the ship
evidence_packet.summary: Arthur Rostron was the captain of RMS Carpathia when it received a morse code message from the ship
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When RMS Titanic hit an iceberg at about 23:40 BST on 14 April 1912, it was not until an hour later that an emergency call went out to other ships in the area The morse code message was picked up by the RMS Carpathia which was on its way to Gibraltar from New York It was captained by Arthur Rostron from Bolton His story is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds Dik Barton, from the British Titanic Society, said it was pure luck the Carpathia received the message in the middle of the night "It was most extraordinary that the Carpathia radio operator picked it up because other vessels in the proximity - the California, for example - the actual radio operator was asleep at the time," he said

The nursery was issued with a prohibition order by Salford Council's environmental health department on Friday, 2 October after inspectors discovered vermin in the Liverpool Road building. title: Warning to drivers as part of M60 to shut for gantries demolition

evidence_packet.title: Warning to drivers as part of M60 to shut for gantries demolition
evidence_packet.lead: Severe congestion is expected while work takes place at Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
evidence_packet.summary: Severe congestion is expected while work takes place at Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning to drivers as part of M60 to shut for gantries demolition - BBC News Image caption, Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday evening By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 9 October 2026 Drivers are being warned of "severe congestion" when a busy stretch of motorway is closed this weekend as part of an upgrade to the road. Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday night until 06:00 on Monday. The closures are to enable the demolition of two large overhead gantries at the Simister Island Interchange. It comes after two others were removed last month. National Highways said the work was part of a £300m improvement scheme and would improve traffic flow, support future housing, employment and growth across the region. Frances Oliver, of National Highways, told BBC North West Tonight : "These gantries are up to 120 tonnes so it's very similar to removing a small footbridge so it is quite a large amount of work for us to undertake." Image caption, Two busy junctions at Simister and Prestwich will be closed for the work Oliver added: "We are expecting there to be severe congestion in the area so we are asking people to plan their journeys, check before they travel and if at all try not to travel or defer their journey. "The message is if you don't need to be in the area please try not to be." Image caption, Frances Oliver asked people to avoid the area while the work is taking place this weekend Full closures and timings From Saturday 10 October to Monday 12 October The M60 westbound will be closed from 22:00 on Saturday to 06:00 on Monday The M60 eastbound will be closed from 23:59 on Saturday to 06:00 on Monday Get in touch Tell us which stories we should cover in Greater Manchest

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plans for new train services between London and Wrexham, Rochdale and Blackpool have been rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) The proposal to add more trains on the West Coast Main Line would "likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers", the regulator said It rejected an application from Wrexham, Shropshire and Midlands Railway (WSMR) for five daily Wrexham to London Euston return services, as well as Lumo's proposal for up to four return services between Rochdale and Euston on weekdays and Saturdays, and three on Sundays Avanti West Coast's plans for additional services between Blackpool and Euston were also denied by the ORR The regulator said: "Gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers "ORR concluded that adding more services into these windows in the timetable for recovery would reduce that resilience, increasing the risk of disruption spreading to other services and affecting more passengers."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way The Mancunian Way: Rats, guns and drugs PLUS: Maresca faces the press Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 19:13, 09 Oct 2026 View 5 Images Police outside the Mini Fingers Day Nursery in Irlam (Image: Manchester Eve It’s been an eventful week at Salford's Mini Fingers nursery. On Monday bosses at the day care centre in Irlam announced it was closing, telling parents the ‘business was struggling’ Then it emerged that wasn’t quite the full story. In fact last Friday Salford council issued a prohibition order after discovering a rat infestation beneath collapsed drains under the baby room In an email sent to parents after the inspection, the nursery manager stated the rats ‘had managed to burrow their way into the main building’. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton man, 43, dies in hospital hours after he was tasered by police The police watchdog said he was injured at the time and refused to drop a pair of scissors he was holding Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 11:27, 09 Oct 20 A man believed to have been suffering from a 'mental health crisis' died in hospital hours after he was tasered by police, a watchdog said today. The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it was investigating after the death of the 43-year-old in Bolton this week In a new statement on Friday, the IOPC said the man was found by officers injured and 'bleeding heavily' on Wednesday evening. He then refused to drop a pair of scissors he was holding, the watchdog added An officer went on to discharge a taser and the man was 'restrained'. The IOPC said he 'lost consciousness and stopped breathing' shortly before midnight on Wednesday, with the officers starting CPR He was taken to hospital, but sadly pronounced dead at 3.01am on Thursday morning (October 8) Greater Manchester Police said it had referred itself to the IOPC after the incident at a house on Somerville Square in Halliwell, Bolton. Now the IOPC has confirmed further details

evidence_packet.lead: Crime The gangster cleared of murder just to be cornered in a north Manchester alleyway He will spend another four years and eight months behind bars after his EncroChat weapons dealing was uncovered Thugs who supplied guns and ammo to gangs are arres Cops swooped on Ibraheem Abd
evidence_packet.summary: Crime The gangster cleared of murder just to be cornered in a north Manchester alleyway He will spend another four years and eight months behind bars after his EncroChat weapons dealing was uncovered Thugs who supplied guns and ammo to gangs are arres Cops swooped on Ibraheem Abd
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime The gangster cleared of murder just to be cornered in a north Manchester alleyway He will spend another four years and eight months behind bars after his EncroChat weapons dealing was uncovered Thugs who supplied guns and ammo to gangs are arres Cops swooped on Ibraheem Abdullah , from Crumpsall, after hacking into the encrypted EncroChat network and uncovering his potentially-deadly deals. Messages showed that the 42-year-old, also known as Dwaine George, and who used the handle 'Tenderpasta', mainly sourced customers Co-defendant Amit Desai, 49 from Leicester, who went by 'Brixonlease', collected cash and sometimes delivered the guns Among the weapons Abudallah obtained were converted Slovakian-made Grand Power G9A blank-firing pistols, which he purchased from another EncroChat user. He and Desai are said to have charged £10,000 and £8,500 for the two weapons In March 2020, Desai supplied half a kilo of cocaine to Abdullah as a down payment to secure more guns, keeping a further 500g so that he could fund the remaining cost of the weapons. He also offered to supply Abdullah with cannabis View 4 Images Ibraheem Abdullah being arrested in Cheetham Hill

It’s a pungent, nauseating, rotting kind of smell. Some describe it as ‘rancid eggs’ or ‘burnt sulphur’, other times it smells like stag The stench that has been wafting over Little Hulton for almost two decades. It can be sniffed at odd hours across the housing estate, outside the schools, and most pungently towards the end of Manchester Road, where a lollipop man stoically carries out his daily duties Earlier this week, complaints about the smell became so numerous, the Environment Agency launched an investigation into its source. But you don’t need to be an expert to figure out where the fetor is coming from - you just need to follow your nose View 5 Images The streets immediately around the Kenny site are the worst affected - but the smell travels across the town. (Image: Manchester Evening News) The stink crescendos around Kenny Waste Management on Lester Road, a commercial rubbish management service that deals with everything from food recycling to hazardous waste and construction rubble, according to its website. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport 'Driving around for 15 minutes, or hobbling over from Sainsbury's': Stepping Hill's parking nightmare As patients hobble across the A6 and staff face fines and street parking battles, Stockport leaders and MPs reveal 'advanced' plans for a n Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 06:36, 10 Oct 2026 Updated 06:53, 10 Oct 2026 “I have spent so much time driving around here, just waiting for someone to come back to their car.” Catherine Cullen’s experience is not unique. Parking at Stockport It reared its head again last week after two innocent drivers who had paid for tickets told the Manchester Evening News they were randomly issued with incorrect fines this summer , which they then had to fight to overturn. Scores of others took to our social media pages in respon After a hiatus during Covid, parking enforcement was reintroduced at the site last October, as the latest bid to get a grip on the issue. Yet patients, staff and local residents have said the situation remains a ‘nightmare’ - primarily due to a lack of spaces There could, however, potentially be some light at the end of the tunnel View 9 Images Catherine Cullen (Image: Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Hannah Spencer says Zack Polanski has her 'full support' after leader loses London by-election The Gorton and Denton MP said the Green party is 'here to stay' Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 22:20, 09 Oct Gorton and Denton MP Hannah Spencer has pledged her 'full support' for Zack Polanski after he was defeated in the by-election in Sir Keir Starmer's former seat yesterday (October 8) The Holborn and St Pancras by-election was triggered on September 1 when the former PM announced his resignation from the seat he had held since 2015 Two days later the Green party leader announced he would be standing in the by-election against other candidates including the Labour leader of Camden borough council, Sagal Abdi-Wali Ms Abdi-Wali was ultimately victorious in the by-election held yesterday, winning the seat with 45pc of the vote, a majority of 3,364 over Mr Polanski who came second with 33pc of the vote But this represented a 22pc increase in vote share compared to the 2024 general election, with Labour's share down by three per cent

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way The Mancunian Way: Rats, guns and drugs PLUS: Maresca faces the press Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 19:13, 09 Oct 2026 View 5 Images Police outside the Mini Fingers Day Nursery in Irlam (Image: Manchester Eve It’s been an eventful week at Salford's Mini Fingers nursery. On Monday bosses at the day care centre in Irlam announced it was closing, telling parents the ‘business was struggling’ Then it emerged that wasn’t quite the full story. In fact last Friday Salford council issued a prohibition order after discovering a rat infestation beneath collapsed drains under the baby room In an email sent to parents after the inspection, the nursery manager stated the rats ‘had managed to burrow their way into the main building’. Then in another remarkable twist, on Wednesday night police raided the now empty building Inside they discovered a gun and a ’substantial quantity’ of ammunition. Two men, aged in their 30s and 50s, were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply cocaine and cannabis They have been taken into police custody for questioning. And the rapid and troubling turn of events has left parents reeling

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A34 Woman, 21, dies in A34 horror with man arrested Two others were taken to hospital Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 17:00, 09 Oct 2026 View Image The Alderley roundabout on the A34 (Image: Google Street View) A woman has died in an horror crash on the A34. Emergency services were called to reports of a smash at the Alderley roundabout on the Melrose Way stretch of the Alderley Edge bypass in Cheshire at around 1am this morning (October 9) On arrival, officers found three passengers inside a black Mazda, the driver of whom had fled on foot, Cheshire Police said. The passengers were all treated by a paramedics Sadly, one, a 21-year-old woman from Macclesfield , died of her injuries at the scene. Her next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers The two other passengers, a 34-year-old woman and a 36-year-old man, both also from Macclesfield, were taken to the hospital. A 36-year-old man from Macclesfield was arrested nearby on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving Police are now appealing for anyone with information that could help their investigation to come forward

The town hall owns nearly 2,100 homes across the borough , but they are not directly managed by the local authority The management of the properties is part of four different deals with some lasting up to 30 years. The local authority did not realise it had to oversee the performance of contractors as the landlord That led to a damning inspection by the Regulator of Social Housing in 2025. The rating related to the council’s oversight rather than the quality of the housing itself The regulator found ‘serious failings’ on the part of the council which required ‘significant improvement’. evidence_packet.summary: Crime The gangster cleared of murder just to be cornered in a north Manchester alleyway He will spend another four years and eight months behind bars after his EncroChat weapons dealing was uncovered Thugs who supplied guns and ammo to gangs are arres Cops swooped on Ibraheem Abd
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime The gangster cleared of murder just to be cornered in a north Manchester alleyway He will spend another four years and eight months behind bars after his EncroChat weapons dealing was uncovered Thugs who supplied guns and ammo to gangs are arres Cops swooped on Ibraheem Abdullah , from Crumpsall, after hacking into the encrypted EncroChat network and uncovering his potentially-deadly deals. Messages showed that the 42-year-old, also known as Dwaine George, and who used the handle 'Tenderpasta', mainly sourced customers Co-defendant Amit Desai, 49 from Leicester, who went by 'Brixonlease', collected cash and sometimes delivered the guns Among the weapons Abudallah obtained were converted Slovakian-made Grand Power G9A blank-firing pistols, which he purchased from another EncroChat user. He and Desai are said to have charged £10,000 and £8,500 for the two weapons In March 2020, Desai supplied half a kilo of cocaine to Abdullah as a down payment to secure more guns, keeping a further 500g so that he could fund the remaining cost of the weapons. He also offered to supply Abdullah with cannabis View 4 Images Ibraheem Abdullah being arrested in Cheetham Hill

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Hannah Spencer says Zack Polanski has her 'full support' after leader loses London by-election The Gorton and Denton MP said the Green party is 'here to stay' Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 22:20, 09 Oct Gorton and Denton MP Hannah Spencer has pledged her 'full support' for Zack Polanski after he was defeated in the by-election in Sir Keir Starmer's former seat yesterday (October 8) The Holborn and St Pancras by-election was triggered on September 1 when the former PM announced his resignation from the seat he had held since 2015 Two days later the Green party leader announced he would be standing in the by-election against other candidates including the Labour leader of Camden borough council, Sagal Abdi-Wali Ms Abdi-Wali was ultimately victorious in the by-election held yesterday, winning the seat with 45pc of the vote, a majority of 3,364 over Mr Polanski who came second with 33pc of the vote But this represented a 22pc increase in vote share compared to the 2024 general election, with Labour's share down by three per cent

On Monday bosses at the day care centre in Irlam announced it was closing, telling parents the ‘business was struggling’ Then it emerged that wasn’t quite the full story. In fact last Friday Salford council issued a prohibition order after discovering a rat infestation beneath collapsed drains under the baby room In an email sent to parents after the inspection, the nursery manager stated the rats ‘had managed to burrow their way into the main building’. Then in another remarkable twist, on Wednesday night police raided the now empty building Inside they discovered a gun and a ’substantial quantity’ of ammunition. Two men, aged in their 30s and 50s, were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply cocaine and cannabis They have been taken into police custody for questioning. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Teen who drowned at Dovestone used cannabis before airbed tragedy, inquest hears Karl Holland died after getting into difficulty in the water at Dovestone Reservoir View 2 Images Karl Holland died at Dovestone Reservoir on July 10, 2026 (Image: Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 17:36, 09 Oct 2026 Updated 17:36, 09 Oct 2026 A teenager who drowned at a Greater Manchester beauty spot had used cannabis before sliding into the water on an airbed, an inquest has heard. Karl James Stua An inquest at Rochdale Coroners' Court heard on Friday (October 9) that Karl had been socialising with friends at the beauty spot on a sunny day when they decided to slide down a slope and into the water on an airbed Assistant coroner Michael Salt found cannabis, which toxicology reports found Karl had used before his death, contributed "more than minimally" to his death Police evidence heard at the inquest stated there were no suspicious circumstances or evidence of third-party involvement in his death. The court also heard there was no evidence that Karl had intended to harm himself Recording a conclusion of misadventure, Mr Salt described the death as a "very sad" loss of a young man

Emergency services were called to reports of a smash at the Alderley roundabout on the Melrose Way stretch of the Alderley Edge bypass in Cheshire at around 1am this morning (October 9) On arrival, officers found three passengers inside a black Mazda, the driver of whom had fled on foot, Cheshire Police said. The passengers were all treated by a paramedics Sadly, one, a 21-year-old woman from Macclesfield , died of her injuries at the scene. Her next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers The two other passengers, a 34-year-old woman and a 36-year-old man, both also from Macclesfield, were taken to the hospital. A 36-year-old man from Macclesfield was arrested nearby on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving Police are now appealing for anyone with information that could help their investigation to come forward

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts 'Cowardly' driver killed parent and son in horror crash two days before Christmas Clair Fitzharris, 42, and son Sam Fitzharris, 15, died at the scene Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 17:21, 08 Oct 2026 Updated 14:55, 09 O A 'cowardly' driver killed a parent and their son in a fatal head-on collision two days before Christmas before blaming the other driver. Andrew Hall, 37, was driving down Ripponden Road, Oldham, when he veered onto the opposite side of the road and smashed into a Nissan carrying Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court heard that in the moments leading up to the collision at around 4pm on December 23, 2023, Hall had been driving at over 90mph. Three seconds beforehand, he had applied emergency braking, resulting in his BMW 5-series travelling at 73mph Witnesses reported Hall to be overtaking other cars as he came off the junction on the M62 to join the road, which is governed by a 50mph speed limit before the collision Sadly, Ms Fitzharris, who used the pronouns they/them, and their son Sam, died from the injuries they sustained. In the aftermath, Hall was taken to hospital and his blood was tested for alcohol, giving a reading of 87 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood. The legal At his sentencing hearing on Thursday, October 8, the family of Ms Fitzharris wept as moving victim impact statements were read to the court

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Gorton A stolen car crashed into a bollard - and a major Greater Manchester crime ring was brought down Two men have been jailed Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 13:43, 09 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Jailed: Hamza Rafique (Image: GMP) A major drugs ring was exposed after a stolen car driven by a 'runner' crashed into a bollard during a police pursuit. Hamza Rafique, who was behind the wheel, fled the scene but was chased and caught by police hiding in a shop, where he was arrested He had attempted to hide a plastic bag containing cannabis, but police found it and the network was uncovered. Rafique, and another man, are now behind bars for their roles in what police called 'a drugs line which distributed across the Greater Manchester area' Louis Williams, 32, of Milne Close, Gorton , has been jailed for four years and ten months. He pleaded guilty to possession with intent to supply Class A drugs, being concerned in the supply of Class A drugs, possession with intent to supply Class B drugs, being concerned in the Rafique, also 32 and of Stamford Road, Manchester, was jailed in July for two years and eight months after admitting possession with intent to supply Class B drugs, dangerous driving, driving otherwise in accordance with licence, driving without insurance, and possession of crimi Both were sentenced at Manchester Crown Court - with Williams jailed earlier this week

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Manchester mum, 33, dies suddenly as devastated family pay tribute to 'beautiful soul' Rachael Hewerdine and her nine-year-old daughter Bonnie were said to 'inseperable' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 12:49, 09 Oct 2 A family have told of their heartbreak after a young mum died unexpectedly from a stroke aged just 33. Rachael Hewerdine, from Manchester , died in hospital on September 29 She leaves daughter Bonnie, aged nine. Rachael's sudden death has devastated her loved ones, with friends remembering her as a 'beautiful soul' and a 'kind girl'. Bonnie is now being cared for by her maternal grandparents, Michelle and Brian Paying tribute, Rachael’s friend Katie said: "I am so, so shocked and saddened to hear of the sad passing of such a beautiful soul at age 33 to a stroke. Rachael leaves behind a nine-year-old little girl, a baby now without her mum "As we all know, funerals are expensive, as will be raising a grandchild for her parents. Rest peacefully, beautiful, kind girl." Rachael’s heartbroken mum, Michelle, said the mother and daughter had been an inseparable team. She added: "It’s such a very sad and shocking event that has left us all shocked and shaken, losing our precious daughter and Bonnie losing her mom. They were a team, Rachael and Bonni

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Apple Watch text that changed a family's life forever "All I have left of the last 20 years of my life is her" View 4 Images Clair Fitzharris and son Sam Fitzharris (Image: Greater Manchester Police) Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 05:59, 09 Oct 2026 Updated 12:39, 09 Oct 2026 It was a drizzly, cold afternoon on December 23, 2023. Martin Fitzharris was busy building his nephew a PC for Christmas . He was expecting his partner, Clair Fitzharris, son, Sa Instead, he received a text that changed his life forever. Clair's Apple Watch, which had him as a named emergency contact, sent him a message to say they had been involved in a collision Within seconds of getting that text he relentlessly tried to call each of them who had been in that car that afternoon, with no success. Eventually someone answered Clair's phone, but it wasn't Clair It was sadly too late. Clair, 42, and Sam, 15, had been killed . His daughter had been left with life-changing injuries that still require surgery to this day Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Andrew Hall had collided with their Nissan on Ripponden Road, Oldham , after veering onto the opposite side of the road. He had been travelling at over 90mph, and overtaken over cards, and braked three seconds before the crash

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it was investigating after the death of the 43-year-old in Bolton this week In a new statement on Friday, the IOPC said the man was found by officers injured and 'bleeding heavily' on Wednesday evening. evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police were called to Bryngs Drive at 11:35 BST on Wednesday over welfare concerns Officers attended and found a person who had died. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The LGBTQ+ bar returns on Tariff Street with cocktails, food, live jazz, drag and late-night DJ sets Go to Manchester's Finest X profile LGBTQ+ cocktail bar Red Light will reopen in Manchester’s Northern Quarter on Friday 9 October, taking over a new space on Tariff Street The bar, founded by Deana Ferguson, will return next door to The Whisky Jar with a new look, an expanded food and drink menu and a programme of live music, DJs and performance The new Red Light features booth seating, a bar and club-style space, red lighting and an outdoor terrace, which will remain open until 11pm. Its interiors will also showcase work from queer local photographers Jen Melia, Sara Carpentieri, Nick Priestley and Harmeet Singh A number of cocktails from Red Light’s original menu will return, including the Pink Picante and Pomme Verte, its take on an appletini. Other returning drinks include the Belfast Coffee, spicy pickle martini Especiado and Pornstar Chic, made with homemade passionfruit sorbet The drinks will be joined by a new snack menu featuring boquerones, pickled guindilla peppers and Gordal olives, alongside Mini Croissant Butter Blondies from Pollen and homemade salted popcorn ice cream

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. However, the striker ultimately stayed at Old Trafford , where he would score in the Champions League final victory over Bayern Munich United host Spurs on Saturday after a two-week international break, a meeting that recalls a transfer agreement which could have taken Solskjaer's career in a different direction. Solskjaer's former team-mate Michael Carrick is now tasked with getting United back on track against Solskjaer, 53, was two seasons into his United career when the clubs agreed a £5.5million fee for his move to Tottenham. That figure was more than three times the £1.5m United had paid Molde to sign him in 1996 but the transfer still required his approval Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! Sir Alex Ferguson's involvement proved decisive, though, as he intervened to remind Solskjaer precisely how highly he rated him. The Norwegian subsequently played a pivotal role in the 1999 Treble the following season, finding the net in United's legendary Champions League final

The feeling we all crave is coming out on top – that kind of sums it up. Whatever’s done in the past tense is in the past, but in that moment is how you feel in that moment. Certainly as a participant, as a perform Carrick was also part of United’s staff under Ole Gunnar Solskjær when they finished second, 22 points behind City, in 2021. City continue to plead their innocence and have appealed against the verdict. If they fail to overturn the independent commission’s ruling, they will proba “It’s affected me personally in different ways,” Carrick said. “But as the case is ongoing now I don’t know where that stands and how it’s going to end up, so we’ll just have to wait and see. Carrick and his United teammates were left solemn on th “The emotion, the feeling about winning, a lot of it is in the moment,” Carrick said. “Whether you’re successful, whether you lose, whether it goes against you, that initial [feeling], the beauty of sport and the beauty of football and the beauty of trying to win trophies here, i “Once that’s done, there’s no getting that back in any direction. The feeling we all crave is coming out on top – that kind of sums it up. Whatever’s done in the past tense is in the past, but in that moment is how you feel in that moment. Certainly as a participant, as a perform Carrick was also part of United’s staff under Ole Gunnar Solskjær when they finished second, 22 points behind City, in 2021. City continue to plead their innocence and have appealed against the verdict. If they fail to overturn the independent commission’s ruling, they will proba “It’s affected me personally in different ways,” Carrick said. “But as the case is ongoing now I don’t know where that stands and how it’s going to end up, so we’ll just have to wait and see. What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone’s benefit is essential.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
